# When does the judge give an answer its evidence does not support? A census of the stored readings (D518, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

Scripts: `inventory_earlier_readings.py` (every answer of the two earlier readings that both first readers did not pass, from the
readers' stored files; `inventory-earlier-readings.json`), `class-by-judgement.json` (the kind of each, written by hand after reading
every one), `tally_unsupported.py` (the counts). Nothing was sent to a model and nothing in either system changed.

## The answer

**Of 438 stored answers that two reader families have read, 36 were settled as unsupported or as resting on too little. 31 of the
36 are one situation: a question that asks for an amount, judged on days when nothing the judge was shown is enough to size it.**
The judge must still name a band, so it names one; the readers say the evidence prefers none. These are 438 readings of answers,
many of them the same question on successive days, not 438 independent cases: the 31 sit on eight question paths and three matters.
On the largest such question the timing is exact: in four runs, every answer of the first five days fails (19 of 20 for this reason,
one for another), and from the day the first sized amount is in view the readers pass every one of the 31 later answers. That is
the observed timing and the readers' verdicts; it does not prove the amount's arrival caused the change, or that every later
scaling is right.

Three more of the 36 are a second situation: the evidence sizes part of the answer and the judge closes the gap with a number of its
own (a discount of one-fifth, a growth rate of 25%, a scaling ratio), and that number decides the band. This is the kind found in
both later readings, and it is the one answer of the fresh week that both teams fail.

| Reading | Judge and questions | Answers read | Settled unsupported | Settled "too little to prefer a band" | Not settled against the answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (D426) | the frozen judge on hand-written questions, July window, three runs, every day's answer | 159 | 4 | 7 | 1 unresolved; 2 split and settled as supported |
| Stage B (D429) | the frozen judge on the new system's own questions, July window, three runs, every day's answer | 236 | 4 | 19 | 12 unresolved; 5 split and settled as supported |
| Trial (D485) | last answers of one run of each system, July window | 21 | 1 | 0 | 3 failed by one team only |
| Fresh week (D489) | last answers of one run of each system | 22 | 1 | 0 | 5 failed by one team only |
| | | **438** | **10** | **26** | 28: 13 unresolved, 7 split at first and settled as supported, 8 failed by one team only |

"Settled" is by each reading's own rule: both first readers, or both third readers where the first differed. The two earlier readings
are taken from their stored reader files and their recorded results (`clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/RESULT.md`,
`STAGE_B_RESULT.md`), where every answer a reader called unsupported was already read by hand; they are not read again here. The
eight answers of the two later readings were read here against their requests. The readings differ in what they read (every day's
answer against last answers only), so the 438 are not one sample and 8% is not a rate for the product.

## By what the answer did

| Kind | Settled (of 36) | Unsupported / too little | Where | Not settled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **N. An amount is asked; nothing shown is enough to size the total (no amount, like deal to scale from, or accounting identity for it; a part may be loosely sized, as "multi-billion"); a band is named anyway** | **31 (86%)** | 5 / 26 | 8 question paths on 3 matters: the total of credit support (19), custom-chip spending (9), memory capacity added in 2027 (3) | 4 |

| C. A figure held flat or carried from the previous answer without being derived again | 0 | | | 4 |
| S. An event with three outcomes; "still open" chosen because neither other outcome is settled today (the new system's questions only) | 1 | 1 / 0 | Kyber shipping | 7 |
| O. One of a kind | 1 | 1 / 0 | money already spent counted as still owed | 3 |

Unsupported alone (10): N 5, B 3, S 1, O 1. Nine of the ten are questions that ask for an amount. The "not settled" column holds
answers left unresolved, answers the first readers split on that were settled as supported, and answers one team alone failed.

N and B are two situations of the evidence (nothing enough to size the total; part sized). They are not shown to be two mechanisms
in the model: an N answer can also rest on an invented bridge, and a B answer on an inference no number explains. One of the three
settled B answers (supply commitments scaled by the revenue ratio) is one where my own earlier read supported the answer against
both first readers; the disagreement stands beside the class.

**The clearest picture (kind N).** "What total of credit support will NVIDIA have committed?" opens on 2026-07-01, when the news says
only that NVIDIA will back two partners' capacity (40,000 and 170,000 GPUs), with no dollar figure. For five days the judge answers

| Run | 07-01 to 07-05 | 07-06 to 07-14 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline, run 1 | 4 too little, 1 unsupported (another reason) | 7 of 7 pass |
| baseline, run 3 | 3 too little, 2 unsupported | 7 of 7 pass |

The other two matters of kind N never receive an amount in the window: custom-chip spending (only one of four programmes is sized,

| S | "'not established' is a statement of confidence, never a reason to stay", against the new system's three-outcome events (D409) | Not read here: the earlier reading left it unresolved between the families. |

article gives none (D398, 7 to 9 of 18 such questions).

## What it costs a reader, where the product is judged

- At the end of the July window, where the frozen judgement reference measures the answer: all 16 last answers of the baseline pass;
  of Stage B's 26, 21 pass, 2 are "too little" (kind N) and 3 are unresolved; the trial has one settled unsupported last answer of

- Kind N costs a reader in a question's first days, and for as long as no amount arrives: the answer shown is a band nothing

- Kind B costs a reader at any time: the band rests on a fraction or a rate the judge chose, and another run chooses another.

- A rate: the earlier readings read every day's answer of 16 and 26 questions; a few questions carry the counts (19 of the 31 are one

- That the readers are right: two model families, whose bars differ (one family alone fails 8 answers of the two later readings; the

- That a change would help. No change has been written or tried, and the judge is frozen.
- The judge's own account of why it names a band with nothing sized, or how it picks a fraction: not asked.

## The stop condition (council round 8), applied

A single situation does account for a counted share: kind N, 31 of 36. What is not established is a common cause, or a correction
that removes that share on stored cases without harming the answers that pass. So nothing is built on this census alone.

# The judge on questions that ask for an amount: what we found, the choice it raises, and why nothing is sent yet (D520, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

## For Alex: the note

**What happens.** When a question asks for an amount ("how much credit support will NVIDIA have committed?") the judge always answers
with a band. Two things go wrong, in both systems, because they share the judge:

1. **Nothing in the news sizes the amount yet, and the judge names a band anyway.** The credit-support question opened on 2026-07-01
   with no dollar figure anywhere. For five days the judge answered "below $5 billion" in some runs and "$1 to 5 billion" in others.
   On 07-06 one partner disclosed a $4.88 billion backstop, and from that day the reviewers pass every answer.
2. **Part of the amount is sized, and the judge closes the gap with a number of its own that decides the band.** On the same question
   it scaled the $4.88 billion to the second partner at full size ($25.6 billion), then at half ($15.3 billion), then at full size
   again, then at one-fifth ($9 billion, a lower band), over eight days of one run. No statement gives any of the fractions.

**How often.** Reviewers have read 438 stored answers. 36 were settled as unsupported or as resting on too little; 31 of the 36 are
the first kind and 3 the second. These are readings of answers, many of them one question on successive days: the 31 sit on eight
question paths and three matters. At the end of the test windows, where an answer matters most: none of 16, 2 of 26 (with 3 more
left unresolved between the reviewers), 1 of 21 and 1 of 22 last answers.

**What the judge says when asked.** Given four of these answers back and asked what led to the band, it said each time that the
band rested on an assumption it had introduced and that the evidence did not give; in the two unsized cases it added that its own
instructions forbade the band it had chosen.

**The choice, which is yours.** Two cases, which need not get the same answer: (1) nothing sizes the amount; (2) an estimate uses a
step nothing supports.
- **A. Leave it.** Every question always shows a band. An unsupported answer can then stay on show; how much of that cost falls in
  a question's first days across the whole product is not measured.
- **B. Show the band with a plain label** of what it rests on ("the judge's own assumption: a one-fifth timing discount"; "nothing
  sizes this yet"). The forecast stays visible. Not shown to work: a forecast legitimately uses calculations and assumptions, so a
  label could mislead or become routine, and whether the judge can mark its own answers reliably is untested.
- **C. Show no band.** In case (1), until something sizes the amount. Doing the same in case (2) is a further choice: it hides a
  forecast an analyst might still want.

The council has no recommendation among these. None is built or tested: any of B or C needs a new version of the judge (today's
is frozen) and a decision on what the product shows. Nothing has changed in either system.

## 1. Where the finding comes from

`UNSUPPORTED-CENSUS.md` (four stored readings joined, the counts, the instructions concerned, the earlier decisions on the ground)
and `ACCOUNT-RESULT.md` (the four accounts in full, $0.0041).

## 2. Two questions, day by day (stored answers; nothing sent)

**Data-center revenue for fiscal 2027, the old system, fresh week.**

| Day | Band | The figure and where it comes from |

| 09-22 | 3 | "A precise FY2027 figure cannot be derived from the supplied evidence"; the $350 to 400 billion band "without a defensible point estimate". |
| 09-23 to 09-26 | 3 | About $393 billion: the first quarter backed out from stated figures ($89 billion and 18% growth give about $75 billion: a derivation), then the 18% carried into the third and fourth quarters (an assumption the instructions ask for: "carries the guided growth forward"). |

| 09-28 | 2 | The same, with the 25% now also standing in the previous answer shown back. Both teams fail this answer. |

| 07-01 to 07-05 | 3 | "Low single-digit billions", with another $3.5 billion guarantee as "a scale anchor, not a confirmed programme total". Nothing sizes the programme. |
| 07-06 | 5 | $25.6 billion: one partner's disclosed $4.88 billion scaled to the other by GPU count (the like-deal sizing the instructions ask for; reviewers pass this step elsewhere). |
| 07-07 to 07-12 | 5 | $15.3 billion: the same with a 50% "execution discount", introduced on 07-07 and repeated for five days. |

What the two tables show: the direction of each change follows real news (a disclosed backstop, an acceleration outlook, a phased
schedule); the size of each estimate is the judge's. The band moved three times: on 07-06, from the third band to the fifth, when
the $4.88 billion comparable arrived, and on 09-27 and 07-14, the two movements the reviewers dispute, each on a day a new
estimate of the judge's own was introduced. On the days an estimate was carried (one day in the first table, five in the second)
the band did not move.

## 3. Can a list of the judge's own assumptions tell a bad answer from a good one? A check on stored answers

Counted by words in the stated figure and reasons ("assume", "discount", "haircut", "allowing", "estimate", "scaled", "carry
forward", "extrapolate"; a rough count by keyword, not a reading):

| | Answers on amount questions | With such a word |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline, passed by the reviewers | 48 | 42 (87%) |
| Baseline, settled unsupported or too little | 11 | 9 |
| Stage B, passed by the reviewers | 85 | 63 (74%) |
| Stage B, settled unsupported or too little | 22 | 18 |

**Most answers the reviewers pass also use such a word.** The count takes words like "estimate" and "scaled", not whether a step is
unsupported, so it is a warning against treating every calculation as an error, not proof that a list of the judge's own steps
could not help a reader. What the reviewers fail is narrower than "an assumption was made": an answer whose band is decided by a
step nothing supports, or one where nothing sizes the amount at all.

## 4. The design, examined against the council's three stop conditions (round 10)

**The idea examined:** the judge's answer gains one required field, written before the band, that says what the band rests on.

| What must be decided or built | Finding |
|---|---|
| What the field says | A plain list of own steps may be filled on most answers (section 3). To separate the failing ones it would have to be a judgement by the judge on its own answer: "the band rests on supplied figures and steps the rules give", "the band is decided by a step of my own" (which, and what the band would be without it), or "nothing shown sizes the amount". That is a three-way classification the model makes: by AGENTS §6 it needs a closed set with examples, which grows the frozen instructions. |
| Whether the judge writes it before choosing | The answer form puts the band first (`rung`), then the reference and the stated figure, then the reasons (`judging.schema_for`). A field's place in the form does not guarantee the model reasons through it first. |
| Every reader of the answer's fields | The store (`views/store.py`, the judgements table); the next day's request, which shows back only the band and the first 800 characters of the reasons (`views/judging.py`); the judgement reference's scorer, which reads the band; the closing record (`pull.py`); the service behind the pages, which reads the reasons (`service.py`, `bundle.py`); tests that pin the form (`tests/test_stance_fields.py`, `test_frozen_questions_and_judgement.py`). A new field needs a column, a place in the next request and a place on the page, or it reaches no reader. |
| Across days | The next request does not show the previous stated figure or any field but the band and 800 characters of reasons. A label would have to be carried by code into the next request, or judged afresh each day. Whether a carried number should count as "the judge's own" once its first evidence is no longer shown is undecided. |
| Against the frozen reference | The reference answers were written with the same habits (a discount for an unshipped product, sizing from a like deal; D263). A label does not change a band, so the judgement score cannot move by it; a rule that changed bands would be a different change and is not proposed. |
| What a test would have to show for a reader | That the label agrees with the reviewers on the 36 failing answers and on a sample of the passing ones, on single answers and along a question's days; that bands on passing answers do not move beyond their own run-to-run variation. A filled field alone would prove nothing. |

**The three stop conditions:**
1. *The field cannot distinguish unsupported steps from legitimate forecasts.* Not shown either way: section 3 is a warning for a
   plain list, and a three-way classification is untested.
2. *Its reader cannot keep the label's origin across days.* Holds as the code stands: the next request shows 800 characters of
   reasons and nothing else. This is a limit of this design, not proof that no design could carry it.
3. *The behaviour needs an unresolved product choice.* Holds: A, B or C above is a choice of what the product shows.

**So, by the council's own rule, nothing is sent now** (council round 11: the decision not to send is right). What exists is the
finding, the two traces, the check of section 3 and the choice for Alex.

## 5. If Alex chooses B or C: the one test that would come first

The stored requests of the failing answers and of an equal number of passing ones, each sent as stored and with the three-way
classification added, three times each; the classification read against the reviewers' verdicts, and the bands of the passing
answers compared with their own repeats. Its size is not worked out: all 36 failing answers with as many passing ones, two
conditions and three sends each, would be 432 judge calls; a selected set would be sized and priced before it is proposed. Before
it: the changed request read whole against the instructions and the reference by a reviewer who did not write it, and its cases
fixed in advance.

"""Blind reading of the six contested answers and two controls (council round 12; $0). Per question: the whole last request,
the answer, and candidate statements not in the request, dated by its day, each with its source passage. Candidates are found by a
text pattern per matter (a hint written by Claude, listed in PATTERNS; code judges nothing). Controls: the July custom-chip answer
with the five facts that moved it in PRD 10's test (a group), and the supply-commitments answer (uncontested) whose candidates
are repeats of statements already shown. Shuffled; the key outside the repository.

  python3 build_trace_packets.py <key folder>
"""
import json
import random
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[3]
RUN = ROOT / 'poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/c1/judge/draw-c1'
JULY = ROOT / 'poc/data/e2e-r9-frozen-v108-2026-11-03/d1'
SEED = 20261117
PATTERNS = {
    'v1': r'guarantee|credit support|backstop|residual[- ]value',
    'v5': r'capex|capital expenditure|capital spending|data[- ]center spending',
    'v10': r'(GW|gigawatt)',
    'v11': r'memory price|DRAM|HBM price|contract price',
    'v12': r'residual[- ]value|\$125 billion|backstop',
    'v13': r'CPO|co-packaged|optical|photonic|Lumentum',
    'v2': r'supply commitment|purchase obligation|\$279 billion',
}
CONTROL_FACTS = ['e219', 'e136', 'e387', 'e153', 'e139']


def last_of(store, archive, view):
    day, sha = store.execute('select publication_day, request_sha256 from judgements where view_id=? order by seq desc, judgement_id desc limit 1', (view,)).fetchone()
    request = json.loads(archive.execute('select request_json from model_calls where request_sha256=?', (sha,)).fetchone()[0])['messages'][-1]['content']
    answer = json.loads(archive.execute('select answer_json from model_calls where request_sha256=?', (sha,)).fetchone()[0])
    return day, request, {k: answer.get(k) for k in ('rung', 'reference', 'reasons', 'implied_outcome')}


def statement(store, evidence_id):
    one_line, quote, who = store.execute('select one_line, quote, original_who from evidence where evidence_id=?', (evidence_id,)).fetchone()
    day = store.execute('select min(publication_day) from evidence_sources where evidence_id=?', (evidence_id,)).fetchone()[0]
    return {'day': day, 'party': who, 'statement': one_line, 'passage': quote}


def main(keys):
    store = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{RUN / 'views.sqlite'}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    archive = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{RUN / 'archive.sqlite'}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    shown = {r['view']: set(r['shown']) for r in json.loads((RUN / 'judge-requests.json').read_text())}
    cases = []
    for view, pattern in PATTERNS.items():
        day, request, answer = last_of(store, archive, view)
        candidates = []
        for evidence_id, one_line in store.execute('select evidence_id, one_line from evidence'):
            if evidence_id in shown[view] or not re.search(pattern, one_line or '', re.I):
                continue
            entry = statement(store, evidence_id)
            if entry['day'] and entry['day'] <= day:
                candidates.append(entry)
        cases.append({'source': view, 'day': day, 'request': request, 'answer': answer, 'candidates': candidates})
    july = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{JULY / 'views.sqlite'}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    july_archive = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{JULY / 'archive.sqlite'}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    day, request, answer = last_of(july, july_archive, 'v16')
    cases.append({'source': 'positive control: July custom-chip v16 (PRD 10 test: these facts moved it 9 of 9)', 'day': day,
                  'request': request, 'answer': answer, 'candidates': [statement(july, e) for e in CONTROL_FACTS]})
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    rng.shuffle(cases)
    for case in cases:
        rng.shuffle(case['candidates'])
    packet = [{'question': f'Q{n}', 'answered_on': c['day'], 'request': c['request'], 'answer': c['answer'],
               'candidates': [dict(s, ref=f'C{k}') for k, s in enumerate(c['candidates'], 1)]} for n, c in enumerate(cases, 1)]
    halves = [packet[:4], packet[4:]]
    for n, half in enumerate(halves, 1):
        path = HERE / f'packet-trace-{n}.json'
        path.write_text(json.dumps(half, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')
        print(f'packet {n}: {[q["question"] for q in half]}, candidates {[len(q["candidates"]) for q in half]}, {len(path.read_text()):,} characters')
    Path(keys).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (Path(keys) / 'key-trace.json').write_text(json.dumps({f'Q{n}': c['source'] for n, c in enumerate(cases, 1)}, indent=1) + '\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1])

**Choose (a) as a bounded diagnostic, starting with a $0 design and control check.** A later account from the judge could help identify a useful lead, but it cannot by itself validate a label the product would show or settle Alex’s choice.

The six-case trace supports a narrower result than its headline. Both families predicted that the **five-fact custom-chip group** would move the control answer and accepted the negative control. Neither predicted that the *selected candidates* would move any of the six answers; both said the residual-value precedent could strengthen confidence in “Yes.” [Trace tally](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/contested-six/tally-trace.txt)

But the candidates came from **patterns over kept summaries**. They do not cover every fact in the fortnight’s articles, every unkept fact, or every kept fact described in different words. The result page’s statement that the contested answers “are not explained by facts the system kept and failed to deliver” should say **“not explained by the candidates selected and read.”** The control demonstrates that these readers could identify that particular group; it does not prove complete retrieval or that other candidate effects are impossible. [Packet builder](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/contested-six/build_trace_packets.py), [trace result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/contested-six/RESULT.md)

I would also keep several conclusions open:

- Both readers identify a form concern on v10, v12 and v13, but “Nvidia publishes no unit counts” is contested in the earlier Stage A reading; it is not established merely by the trace. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt)
- The same earlier answer can receive different judgements: the fresh trace readers both say v1 follows, while one earlier reader rejected its treatment of a cap as an amount. That is a substantive dispute, not a settled mechanism. [Trace tally](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/contested-six/tally-trace.txt), [answer tally](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-run/tally-answers.txt)
- Production remains blocked by the unmet gate and uncompleted integration, alongside contested answer quality. Deck 1 and the gate’s role remain Alex’s pending decisions under D560. “No bounded repair on the record” is accurate; it is not proof that no repair exists. [New-system frame](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md), [D560](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7047)

**Why (a) needs a narrower claim.** A continued conversation asks the model to review an answer *after it made it*. The four previous accounts explicitly warn that this may be a rationalisation and does not show the model would produce the same assessment while answering. A successful test would justify investigating a label; it would not prove the live judge can emit it, that the page carries it correctly, or that it survives the next day. A failed test would reject this particular follow-up question and sample, not every possible label design. [Four accounts](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unsupported/ACCOUNT-RESULT.md), [D520 design note](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unsupported/DESIGN-NOTE.md)

The **passed comparison set is not yet defined by D519’s inventory**. Its earlier-reading inventory deliberately excludes answers both first readers passed. Recover those answers and their original marks from the underlying reading packets and keys, then fix a matched selection before asking the judge: match by question path, date or evidence stage, and answer type where possible. Keep repeated days of the same matter together when assessing results; they are not independent cases. [Inventory code](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unsupported/inventory_earlier_readings.py), [D519 census](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unsupported/UNSUPPORTED-CENSUS.md)

Do not use **“no better than 87% against ~80%”** as the falsifier. Those numbers are different keyword frequencies within passed and failed groups, not a single accuracy measure or a matched comparison. First run the keyword rule on the exact proposed cases, define which output counts as a warning, and report false alarms on passed answers and misses on failed answers separately.

The one decision I recommend is therefore: **prepare (a) at $0, with the matched cases, exact reconstructed conversations, scoring rule and same-case keyword baseline frozen; proceed to the cents-bounded account test only if those checks establish that it can discriminate a result.** Keep (c) as an unproved candidate: the residual-value omission is a real delivery lead, but a confidence prediction and D511’s inconclusive send do not establish the benefit of widening later linking.

CONSENSUS: no, because (a) is not yet a defined matched test, and its proposed falsifier would compare unlike keyword counts. The narrower diagnostic above is the direction I support.
